4 14-08-2024 I.A. No.02 of 2024 Heard learned counsel for the appellant, the informant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.
2. This interlocutory application has been filed on behalf of the appellant seeking suspension of his sentence and release on bail during pendency of the appeal.

3. The appellant has been convicted and sentenced vide judgment and order dated 10.09.2021 and 16.09.2021 respectively passed by the learned Additional District and Sessions Judge-VII-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), West Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.452 of 2024(4)
dt.14-08-2024 Champaran, Bettiah in CIS-65 of 2018 arising out of Dhanha P.S. Case No. 161 of 2018 for the offences punishable under Sections 341, 376 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code (in short 'IPC') and Section 6 of the Protection Of Children From Sexual Offences Act (in short 'POCSO Act')

sentences.text: All the sentences shall run concurrently.
4. As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the appellant is that he had committed rape upon the informant.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits with reference to the evidence of the victim girl (PW-1)
that from her statements in paragraph '15', '16' and '17' of her depositions, it would appear that it is a case of adolescence relationship outside of the marriage.
The victim claims that 10-15 days earlier she was subjected to rape in a field which is situated at a distance of Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB)
No.452 of 2024(4) dt.14-08-2024 two kms from her house.
She has stated that she had gone there after receiving a message from this appellant that the monkeys are destroying her field.

The appellant had met her at 2.00 PM whereafter she had gone to the field at a distance of two kms and she has stated that she had not given any information with regard to her going to the field to her uncle and aunt.
6.
Learned counsel submits that the appellant and the victim girl both were in relationship and they were thinking to marry for which they had gone to the temple.
The victim girl has also stated that she had called the appellant in Khirkiya temple on the pretext of marriage.
She has stated that in the temple, her parents and the parents of the appellant and other persons were also present.
She denied the suggestion that the parents of the appellant had given her clothes.
PW-1 has stated that police had come at the temple, however, no marriage was solemnized, she had called the appellant and got him arrested by police.

7. Learned counsel submits that in paragraph '21' of her deposition, the victim girl has stated about some photographs but when she was suggested about those photographs with the appellant, she claims that those photographs were taken under pressure.
These materials on the record, according to learned counsel for the appellant, would Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.452 of 2024(4)
dt.14-08-2024 show that the appellant and the victim girl (PW-1) were close to each other but because the appellant belongs to a member of scheduled caste, the family members of the victim girl did not like him and got him arrested.
8. Learned counsel further submits that the age of the victim girl has not been duly proved as required under the POCSO Act.

In this connection, learned counsel has referred the evidence of the I.O. (PW-4) who has stated in paragraph '12' of his cross-examination that apart from the doctor's opinion, he had not collected any evidence as regards the age of the victim.
Referring to the medical examination report which has been proved by PW-5, learned counsel submits that the doctor has opined that the age of the victim would fall somewhere between 17 to 19 years.

It is submitted that in absence of proper determination of the age of the victim as required in law and on the face of the opinion of the medical board with regard to her age, the prosecution could not establish the basic Arjun Sahani vs The State Of Bihar on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49847482/
2 fact that the victim (PW-1) was a child within the meaning of the POCSO Act.

sentences.text: It is submitted that she had attained majority.
The doctor had not found any injury on the body of the victim and according to the doctor the hymen was ruptured old.
Spermatozoa was not seen in vaginal swab and there was no recent sign of sexual assault.
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.452 of 2024(4) dt.14-08-2024 9.

It is submitted that the I.O. has tried to shift the place of arrest of the appellant by making statement in his evidence that the appellant was arrested on the basis of a secret information from Basi Chowk whereas the victim has herself stated that she got the appellant apprehended by calling him in the temple.

10. It is further pointed out that one defence witness has come on behalf of the appellant in this case and he has stated that the marriage between the appellant and the victim was being opposed by the villagers because they were going to solemnize inter-caste marriage.
11. The prayer of the appellant for bail has been opposed by learned counsel for the informant as well as learned Addl. P.P. for the State.
It is submitted that PW-1 and other prosecution witnesses have supported the prosecution case.

Learned counsel for the informant has submitted that the victim had studied in a school, however, the school admission register could not be produced and the age of the victim was proved on the basis of a record of the gram panchayat.

12. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and learned Addl.P.P. for the State as also on a prima-facie perusal of the records, this Court finds from the deposition of the victim Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.452 of 2024(4) dt.14-08-2024 girl itself that it seems to be a case of adolescence relationship outside of marriage as both the victim and the appellant are in the same age group, the age of the victim girl has not been duly proved in accordance with Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 which would be applicable in case of a POCSO victim, the place of arrest is a temple where the appellant was called by PW-1 and PW-1 has stated that in the temple parents of both the sides were present, this gives an impression to this Court that the suggestion given by the defence in course of trial is carrying some weight which may be required to be considered at final hearing of the case but on the face of all these materials and that the appellant has already remained in custody for over three years eight months altogether but this appeal is not likely to be heard in near future, we direct suspension of sentence and release of the appellant on bail, during pendency of the appeal, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/-(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional District and Sessions Judge-VII-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), West Champaran, Bettiah in connection with CIS-65 of 2018 arising out of Dhanha P.S. Case No. 161 of 2018.
